name: mib问题处理.docx
method: python-docx(段落+表格+文本框+页眉页脚)
text:
Question:
1\ Ok, the switch returns a few extra SNMP values which do not resolve with the provided MIB files, what are these values:
SNMPv2-SMI::enterprises.56813.5.25.31.1.1.3.1.5.2 = INTEGER: -255
SNMPv2-SMI::enterprises.56813.5.25.31.1.1.3.1.5.3 = INTEGER: -255
……
and
SNMPv2-SMI::enterprises.171.12.58.1.1.1.8.2 = INTEGER: 0
SNMPv2-SMI::enterprises.171.12.58.1.1.1.8.3 = INTEGER: 0
……
and
NMS-SYS-MIB::sys.4.1.1.1 = INTEGER: 1
NMS-SYS-MIB::sys.4.1.2.1 = INTEGER: 48
Please share these missing MIB files.
Reply: The 1.3.6.1.4.1.56813* and 1.3.6.1.4.1.171* SNMP values have been removed.
Updated NMS-SYS-MIB to provide definitions for NMS-SYS-MIB::sys.4.1.1 and NMS-SYS-MIB::sys.4.1.2.
2\ The MIB enterprise IDs (.1.3.6.1.4.1.57430.* and .1.3.6.1.4.1.56813.* and .1.3.6.1.4.1.171.*)) are registered to two other companies:
Dongguan Huarong Communication Technologies Co., Ltd.
Fuzhou Dockeer Technology Co., Ltd.
D-Link Systems, Inc.
How is smart bytes/saga telecom related to these companies?
Reply:
3\ lldpV2RemPortDesc contains a trailing zero byte, e.g.:
LLDP-V2-MIB::lldpV2RemPortDesc.0.27.1.3 = STRING: tengigabitEthernet0/28\x00
Reply: The trailing zeros are removed in the new version.
4\ Our monitoring system is picking up an error
Our monitoring system is picking up an error from this (This is probably just a misconfiguration):
UCD-SNMP-MIB::memCached.0 = INTEGER: 30564 kB
UCD-SNMP-MIB::memSwapError.0 = INTEGER: error(1)
UCD-SNMP-MIB::memSwapErrorMsg.0 = STRING: Running out of swap space (0)
Reply: We will not support UCD-SNMP-MIB in the new version
Suggestion:
Did you just create the MIB files with the last software version?
Because with the current layout e.g. the optical MIB is not suitable for multi lane optics (e.g. most 40G, 100G transceivers) where DDM will provide data for each lane. If it’s newly designed I would suggest you update your design before it’s deployed to more customers.
Reply: not support 40G, 100G now
Unique OID for each hardware series/model
It’s best practice to set SNMPv2-MIB::sysObjectID.0 to a unique OID for each hardware series/model, see e.g. the juniper product MIB here:
https://mibs.observium.org/mib/JUNIPER-CHASSIS-DEFINES-MIB/
Currently it’s set to a fixed value:
SNMPv2-MIB::sysObjectID.0 = OID: NMS::nms
Reply: not support, we are OEM factory
